```console
1
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Running a new language model on every benchmark is costly, yet leaderboards hold many earlier scores. We ask which $k$ benchmarks to run on a new model so that its remaining scores can be inferred, and how large $k$ must be. We study factor-model prediction with greedy Bayesian A-optimal selection (it chooses benchmarks one at a time to minimise the average posterior variance of the unrun scores) under a protocol that holds out whole model families, fits before selecting, and uses paired, family-clustered intervals, on dense blocks of MTEB embedding-model results and the 57 subjects of HELM MMLU, and on MTEB matrices with missing cells; we do not test suites of benchmarks for generative language models. Three benchmarks close 81--96\% of the gap between the column-mean predictor and a leave-one-benchmark-out predictor, but 90\% needs one benchmark on HELM MMLU and nine or more on MTEB, with wide intervals. Greedy selection beats random selection by 6--11\% of the error, mostly at $k\le3$, and meets our pre-specified 10\% margin on one pool of three; with missing cells (21--70\% observed) it closes 0.71--0.80 of the gap at $k=3$ with the pairwise-correlation predictor, against 0.55--0.74 for random. Later and stronger models are predicted worse and too low. A closed-form risk is exact with known parameters and gives the shape of the error-versus-$k$ curve, but its level is 36--69\% off on real data.
\end{abstract}
```

shown.message:
PR #9 now holds both rounds of review fixes. Idea and venue still have changes requested on the earlier head and I've asked them to look again. I'm ending the turn until they and `figtab-repo` respond.

- **Story review (#10):**
  - Section 6.3 now says the factor model buys no accuracy over simple predictors, the selector's gain is modest and shared by simpler selectors, and the formula gives shape only.
  - Section 7 drops "a k chosen on random splits is too small" and ends its takeaway with the answer to how large k must be.
- **Idea review:**
  - The abstract and introduction now name the data (MTEB embedding-model results, the 57 HELM MMLU subjects) and say we do not test suites of benchmarks for generative language models.
  - Related work now says "Among the work we read, none treats…".
  - The abstract says the selector chooses benchmarks one at a time.
  - I did not take idea's two optional items (citing sources for the baselines, a clause on adaptive testing).
- **Venue review:** I added the typewriter-font line (`\renewcommand{\ttdefault}{pcr}`). `pdffonts` on my build shows no Type 3 font.
- **Figures and tables:** I took `figtab-repo`'s compact main-text Table 3 and its appendix table by k, and the appendix now cites them.
- **Length:**
  - The main text still ends on page 9, and the PDF is 26 pages.
  - To fit the added scope sentences I cut the introduction's overview of earlier work and point to Related work instead.
  - The abstract is about 220 words, longer than the 150–200 I aimed for. I trimmed it but not that far.
- **Requests to `figtab-repo`:** drop the file name from the `tab:sparse-k` caption, remove the superseded `tableA6_sparse.tex`, and review the new head.
- **Approvals:** the story and experiment approvals were given on an earlier head, which I then changed. Whether they stand is unchecked.
- **Next:** once PR #9 merges into `main`, I merge `main` into PR #7 (the `final` PR) and ask `internal-review-repo` to review again.
